notes.summary: Reasoning & Mental Ability in WBCS Prelims tests verbal and non-verbal logic: series, analogy, classification, coding-decoding, blood relations, directions, ranking, seating, calendars, clocks, syllogisms, Venn diagrams and symbol substitution. The questions are short and follow standard patterns, so speed comes from knowing those patterns and shortcuts.
keyPoints: Alphabet positions: remember EJOTY (E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25). Position from the end = 27 - position, so M (13th) is 14th from the end.

Series: check the differences (constant, rising, squares), the ratios (×2, ×3) and alternate terms. In two-letter groups, treat each letter separately: AZ, CX, EV means the first letter goes +2 and the second -2.
Ranking: position from the other end = total - given position + 1, so 12th from the left in a row of 40 is 29th from the right. Total = left rank + right rank - 1.

Calendar: an ordinary year has 1 odd day and a leap year 2. A date moves forward 1 weekday the next year, or 2 if 29 February falls in between. A century year is a leap year only if it is divisible by 400.
Clocks: the minute hand moves 6° per minute and the hour hand 0.5°. Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. The hands coincide at 60H/11 minutes past H, so after 3 o'clock they meet at 16 4/11 minutes past 3.
Syllogism: All + All = All, and Some + All = Some. All + Some gives no definite conclusion. 'Some A are B' never proves 'All B are A'.
Sets: n(A or B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(both), and neither = total - n(A or B).
Blood relations and coded relations: decode one symbol at a time and draw a family tree, marking + for male and - for female. Settle each person's gender before naming the relation.
Direction: use Pythagoras for the straight-line distance (watch for the 3-4-5 triangle). Turning right while facing north means facing east.
Symbol substitution: replace every sign first, then apply BODMAS, so division and multiplication come before addition and subtraction.
traps: Working left to right after substituting symbols, without applying BODMAS.
Forgetting that a one-year span containing 29 February has 2 odd days, not 1.
Reading 'Some pens are tables' as 'All tables are pens'. A 'Some' statement never turns into an 'All' statement.
Forgetting the +1 in ranking. 40 - 12 = 28 is wrong; the answer is 29th.
Assuming someone's gender from their name instead of from the clues in a blood-relation question.
notes.examTip: For any arrangement, ranking or blood-relation question, sketch the row, order or family tree on your rough sheet first. Re-reading the clues without a diagram costs more time than drawing it.

questions.text: In the English alphabet, which letter is 7th to the right of the 12th letter from the left end?
questions.explanation:
The 12th letter from the left is L.
The 7th letter to its right is at position 12 + 7 = 19.
The 19th letter is S. (EJOTY: T = 20, so 19 is S.)
Counting to the left instead gives 12 - 7 = 5, which is E.
Answer: S.

questions.text:
Find the odd one out:
Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Rhombus
questions.explanation:
A square, a rectangle and a rhombus all have four sides, so they are quadrilaterals.
A triangle has only three sides.
Answer: Triangle.

questions.text:
Find the next term in the series:
AZ, CX, EV, GT, ?
questions.explanation:
First letters: A, C, E, G go up by 2 each time, so the next is I.
Second letters: Z, X, V, T go down by 2 each time, so the next is R.
Answer: IR.

questions.text: 15 August 2023 was a Tuesday. On which day of the week did 15 August 2024 fall?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The period from 15 August 2023 to 15 August 2024 includes 29 February 2024, so it has 366 days.
Step 2: 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days, so there are 2 odd days.
Step 3: Tuesday + 2 days = Thursday.
Ignoring the leap day gives Wednesday, which is the common mistake.
Answer: Thursday.

questions.text:
If '+' means '×', '−' means '+', '×' means '÷' and '÷' means '−', what is the value of:
8 + 3 − 12 × 4 ÷ 5
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Replace the signs: 8 × 3 + 12 ÷ 4 − 5.
Step 2: Multiplication and division first: 8 × 3 = 24 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
Step 3: Then addition and subtraction: 24 + 3 − 5 = 22.
Working left to right without BODMAS gives 4, which is wrong.
Answer: 22.

questions.text: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T are sitting in a row facing north. R is sitting in the middle. P is at the extreme left end. T is sitting immediately to the right of P. Q is not at either end. Who is sitting at the extreme right end?
questions.explanation:
Number the seats 1 to 5 from the left.
P is at 1, and T, immediately to P's right, is at 2.
R, in the middle, is at 3.
Q is not at an end, so Q takes seat 4, which leaves seat 5 for S.
The row is P T R Q S.
Answer: S.

questions.text: Among five boys A, B, C, D and E, A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is taller than C. E is the shortest of all. Who is the second tallest?
questions.explanation:
From the first clue: C > A > B.
D is taller than C, so D > C > A > B.
E is the shortest, so the full order is D > C > A > B > E.
The second tallest is C.
Answer: C.

questions.text:
Statements:
Some pens are books.
All books are tables.
Conclusions:
I. Some pens are tables.
II. All tables are pens.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation:
The pens that are books lie inside 'books', and every book is a table, so those pens are tables. Conclusion I follows (Some + All = Some).
Nothing says that every table is a pen, and tables can exist outside the set of pens. Conclusion II does not follow.
Answer: Only conclusion I follows.

questions.text: In a group of 60 people, 35 like tea, 30 like coffee and 10 like both tea and coffee. How many people like neither tea nor coffee?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: People who like at least one = 35 + 30 − 10 = 55. (The 10 who like both were counted twice.)
Step 2: Neither = 60 − 55 = 5.
Answer: 5.

questions.text: At what time between 3 o'clock and 4 o'clock will the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock coincide?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: At 3:00 the hour hand is 3 × 30° = 90° ahead of the minute hand.
Step 2: The minute hand gains 6° − 0.5° = 5.5° on the hour hand every minute.
Step 3: Time to close the 90° gap = 90 ÷ 5.5 = 180/11 = 16 4/11 minutes.
Shortcut: the hands coincide at 60H/11 minutes past H, and 60 × 3 / 11 = 16 4/11.
Answer: 16 4/11 minutes past 3.

questions.text: In a certain code, 'P + Q' means P is the father of Q, 'P − Q' means P is the wife of Q, and 'P × Q' means P is the brother of Q. If A − B + C × D, how is A related to D?
questions.explanation:
A − B: A is the wife of B.
B + C: B is the father of C.
C × D: C is the brother of D, so D is also B's child.
A is the wife of D's father, so A is D's mother.
Answer: Mother.
